matchups.recap:
Funk that Junk ran this week's cookout like a well-oiled grill, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba torching the field for 27.1 and Deebo Samuel Sr. right behind him at 24.4, both carrying the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike while Drake Maye sat on the sidelines eating his trail cheese and salami at a measly 3.02. Old Balls shrugged off the quarterback no-show because the receivers more than covered the woodpile, and the whole cabin cruised to a well-earned Tuna Casserole without much sweat.

Rome-ans 10:9-10 came into the lodge with a decent fire going — Drew Lock, Josh Downs, and Aaron Jones Sr. all pulled their weight — but Jaylen Warren and Travis Kelce Stole my wow, limping to 6.6 and 4.0 against projections that promised so much more. The Lone Eagle's bench stayed stocked with Beak decisions nobody needed, and even without a disaster at the top, 82.7 wasn't enough to out-hike a cabin that had its gear packed and ready. Final whistle: Funk that Junk by 18.82, Boss planning against a camp that got caught bushwhacking without a compass at the skill positions.

Counsel ran the activity with a plan built around Jahmyr Gibbs, who carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike with 40.7, got some help from Chuba Hubbard trotting like a woodsman running to the camp store on his way to 31.7, and Trevor Lawrence chipping in 26.78 to keep the canoe moving. A.J. Brown and Denzel Boston spent the afternoon bushwhacking without a compass, combining for under six points against a projected twenty-plus, but 55 Burgers still went on a Bust Hike and got the sticky buns on Sunday morning anyway.

Blue Ridge got a Guide Rec performance out of Ja'Marr Chase and Isaiah Likely, with C.J. Stroud chipping in a respectable 20.44, but the final arithmetic left Harley Jarvis stuck in the Sewards by 6.44 points. The margin stings worse knowing both cabins left points folded in their sleeping bags, but Counsel's plan simply had fewer holes to patch with leaves — Blue Ridge's crew got soaking wet while Counsel stayed dry and claimed the well-earned Tuna Casserole.

George Pickens went like a woodsman running to the camp store all afternoon, finishing with 38.0, and Patrick Mahomes tagged along for 35.42 as Catalina Wine Mixon's craft period turned into a full-blown Penis Eating Pike. The Chair Force had every arrow in the bullseye this week, mixing Cam Skattebo's 25.7 into the pile until Team Bradford's cabin had no answer left to give. That's a post hike scrub by any measure, and sticky buns on Sunday Morning for the whole lodge.

Team Bradford, meanwhile, chose the Canoe Hike and never found the trailhead. DeMario Douglas and Jalen Coker combined for a grand total of 1.2 points, soaking wet and useless, while Emmett Johnson's 32.1 carried the load like a Woodsman Chief on a hike all by himself with nobody else showing up to help haul gear. Team No Creativity is stuck on the Point and Back now, losers of two straight, and the counselor's weekly planning session is starting to look like bushwhacking without a compass. Time to redraw the map before next week's hike.

matchups.winner: Chase Brown Had a Bad Scare
matchups.recap:
Christian McCaffrey put together a hike plan worth bragging about at lineup, dragging 44.3 points back to camp while Brock Purdy and Chase Brown carried the load like Woodsmen Chiefs behind him. Pill Pusher had all the arrows in the bullseye this week, and even a Dutch Oven afternoon from Chris Olave couldn't slow the march to a 41.56-point post hike scrub. This was never a tug of war, it was a canoe with one paddler.

Ricky Huns, meanwhile, is stuck on the Point and Back for a second straight week, and the trail cheese and salami treatment found Kyren Williams this time, four points on a nearly-seventeen-point projection. Bryce Young had his lunch eaten by Yellow Yellow at the position that was supposed to steer the whole canoe, and Blake Corum's 19.4 was the lone bright spot in an otherwise Bushwhacking-without-a-compass afternoon. Other Nate needs a new map before next week, because this one was Beak from the first whistle.

Joe Burrow turned in a 33.16 clinic through the air while the 46er sat back with a clipboard and let Amon-Ra St. Brown and Bhayshul Tuten carry the load like Woodsman Chiefs on a hike. Even Christian Watson and Tyler Warren going quiet on the trail couldn't dent a performance this Boss — The Island Gudge had all the arrows in the bullseye again, and this camp is starting to feel like it's run by a Pioneer in Gaga ball who simply doesn't lose.

The Machine Knows, meanwhile, got walked straight into the alpine vegetation. Josh Allen's 22.34 and a surprisingly Boss night from the Vikings D/ST were the only things keeping this from total silence, because Malik Nabers and Sam LaPorta spent the afternoon stuck in the Sewards, nowhere near their projections. Forty-three and a half points is the kind of margin that makes a counselor rethink the whole week's plan — this one looked like a Woodsman playing Chief Tyler Hallenbeck in Tetherball, and the scoreboard never once pretended otherwise.

Love Thy Naber posted the largest margin of victory in camp this week, and it showed from the first drill. Parker Washington led the charge at 24.7, James Cook III ran like a woodsman running to the camp store on his way to 21.7, and Jayden Daniels chipped in 20.76 as the whole cabin had all the arrows in the bullseye. Whichever nickname you want to use for this counselor's planning, the word is Boss — this was a Pioneer in Gaga ball afternoon, and somewhere on the hill I want you to BRING DOWN THE ROOF for a cabin that simply had no business losing this one.

Meanwhile Mr. Stefanowicki's Goose is Loose cabin got Dak Prescott's 34.42 and not much else worth writing home about. Tetairoa McMillan, Jakobi Meyers, and Brock Bowers combined to look like a stunned naval battle queen, soaking wet and directionless, and the whole outfit is stuck on the Point and Back as the losing streak stretches on. Bushwhacking without a compass is generous for a week where the backup plan needed a backup plan.

headline: Week 10 brings blowouts, upsets, and one very loose goose
